newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan reactor may restart Thursday--govt official.
newsitem.headline: Japan reactor may restart Thursday--govt official.

text.p: Japan's "Fugen" prototype nuclear reactor, which has been shut since April after officials failed to report an accident promptly, is expected to resume operations as early as Thursday, a government official said on Tuesday.

On Tuesday morning, the Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC), which operates the 165,000-kilowatt reactor, submitted a report to the Science and Technology Agency on measures to be taken to improve the flow of information from the PNC.
An agency official quoted Riichiro Chikaoka, director general of the agency, as saying the proposed measures were adequate and that the time is right to restart the reactor.
"After completing some mandatory paper work, the reactor is expected to be put back on line as early as June 5," the official said.

On April 15, the Science and Technology Agency ordered the PNC to halt operations of the reactor on the Sea of Japan coast after learning the state-run firm had waited 30 hours before reporting a radiation leak at the plant, which had occured the previous day.
The Fugen prototype nuclear reactor provides electricity to to Kansai Electric Power Co Inc, Chubu Electric Power Co Inc and Hokuriku Electric Power Co Inc, a PNC official said.
